text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Tuesday.

LONDON - A rebound in U.S. stocks and bonds helped UK stocks recover from the day's lows by the close, in a day overshadowed by U.S. interest rate fears and worries over the impact of an outbreak of hostilities in Iraq.The FTSE 100 index ended 28.5 points lower at 3,855.9, after rallying from a midsession 48-point tumble.

FRANKFURT - German shares closed bourse trade lower extending losses in last hour of bourse trade ahead of raft of U.S. indicators due to published this afternoon and with sentiment generally weakened after the U.S. missile strike against Iraq, buying also continues to be held back by weaker debt. The 30-share DAX index closed 22.11 points lower at 2,510.77. In post-bourse trade the DAX index stood at 2,528.73.

PARIS - French stocks fell but finished well above their session lows as reassuring U.S. economic data offset some of the nervousness triggered by a U.S. missile attack on Iraqi military targets, the strength of oil shares, buoyed by higher oil prices on the back of the U.S. missile raid, also helped shore up the bourse. The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished down 5.55 points or 0.28 percent to 1,971.43.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended weaker but above session lows, prices were hit early in the day by fears of higher inflation, linked to worries that oil prices will rise in the wake of U.S. cruise missile attacks on Iraqi air defence targets, strong U.S. economic data added to the negative sentiment, with markets nervous before U.S. August jobs numbers on Friday. The All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) retreated 18.59 points or 0.79 percent to 2,327.78.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks swung back to positive territory by the close, but the market did not have an opportunity to react to news that the United States had launched a missile attack against Iraq. The key 225-share Nikkei average closed up 91.04 points or 0.45 percent to 20,198.15.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks ended sharply lower after the U.S. launched cruise missile strikes against targets in Iraq, adding more negative sentiment to a market already suffering from interest rate woes. The Hang Seng index ended 149.39 points lower at 10,957.18.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market closed lower, dragged down by a battered bond market that had its hopes for further local interest rate cuts dashed by much stronger than expected July retail data, speculation on a larger than expected rate hike by the U.S. Federal Reserve also depressed bond market sentiment. By closing, the All Ordinaries index had fallen 12.1 points to 2,244.6.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares reversed early morning gains to end lower on the back of a weak Wall Street opening and as local futures players unwound positions ahead of the September 16 close-out, golds were firmer on a better bullion price, a follow-through of Monday's futures linked buying initially buoyed industrial shares, before nervousness on the Iraq crisis crept in sending industrials sliding. The Overall index lost 29.9 points to 6,705.1, the Industrial index shed 52.9 points to 7,858.9 and the Gold index added 6.5 points to 1,806.4.
